features.name: Basic swiping and board movement
steps: Swipe up, down, left, and right in the board area
All movable tiles compress in the corresponding direction
features.expected: All tiles should move as a whole along the swipe direction to the farthest reachable position; tiles must not pass through other tiles; an invalid swipe must not wrongly change the board

features.name: Identical numbers merge
steps: Construct two identical numbers in the same row/column
Swipe in the direction that brings them together
Two tiles merge into twice the value, e.g. 2+2
features.expected: Only identical numbers can merge; the new tile's value must be the sum of the two; different numbers must not merge; after merging, the visual color/number changes with the value

features.name: Merge-order rules within a single swipe
steps: Construct a row/column with several mergeable tiles, e.g. 2,2,2,2 or 4,4,8
features.expected: This is one of the most important pieces of logic in the reproduction. A tile newly generated during a move must not take part in a second merge within the same move; e.g. 2,2,2,2 should give two 4s, not directly an 8; the merge order must be determined by the swipe direction

features.name: New tile generation after a valid move
steps: Perform a swipe that changes the board
Generate a new low-value tile in a remaining empty cell
Operate repeatedly and observe the random position changes
features.expected: New tiles may only be generated in empty cells; the number generated per valid move should match the target app's behavior, usually 2 or 4; the random position must not overwrite an existing tile

features.name: Handling of invalid moves
steps: Construct a state in which no movement or merge can occur in a direction
Check the board and statistics state
features.expected: An invalid swipe should not change the board or generate new tiles without reason; business states such as scoring must not be wrongly updated

features.name: Score, high score, and game statistics
steps: Observe the score, best, RETRIES, timer, and other statistics fields at the top
Compare again after restarting or starting a new game
features.expected: After merging, the score should accumulate according to the game rules; the high score is correctly maintained across the current game's changes; the screenshot also shows OE, RETRIES, and timing statistics, whose observable state changes should be reproduced

features.name: Reaching 2048 and continuing the challenge
steps: Keep merging from a new game
Verify the state after reaching the goal
If the app allows continuing, keep generating larger tiles
features.expected: The game guide explicitly states that "merging to 2048 is the first step to victory", so the game must not simply force an end when 2048 appears; it must support continuing toward larger values such as 4096 and 8192 while keeping the scoring/board logic correct

features.name: Game-over detection and restarting
steps: Keep playing until the board has no empty cells and no horizontally/vertically mergeable adjacent tiles
features.expected: Game Over must be judged by the absence of any legal move rather than merely whether the board is full; after the end state pops up the old board is kept; replaying re-initializes the board, score, and current-game state

features.name: Undo and state restoration
steps: Restore the board from before the last move
features.expected: Undo should restore the tile positions, values, random new tiles, score, and other related states rather than only the visuals; with no history the button should be unavailable or have no effect; the undo stack after performing a new operation must also update correctly

features.name: Pause and resume
steps: The board enters the paused state
Wait for a period of time
features.expected: The board cannot continue to be modified during a pause; whether the game timer stops must match the target; after resuming, the board and statistics from before the pause are preserved

features.name: Restart the current game
steps: Confirm that the current game is replaced with a new board
features.expected: After restarting the tiles are regenerated and the current game's score/time reset; persistent states such as the global high score must not be wrongly cleared

features.name: Bookmark / game-state save and restore
steps: The game has progressed to an intermediate state
Record the current game via the bookmark/save entry
Continue changing the board or exit
Reload via "go to bookmark" or the corresponding restore entry
features.expected: What is saved should not be merely a board screenshot but the complete game state: board matrix, score, statistics, time, and the necessary resumable state; after restoring, swiping should continue normally

features.name: Recent game history
steps: Complete, exit, or save several games
Choose a record to enter/resume the corresponding game
features.expected: The screenshot clearly shows "last modified" and "elapsed time"; multiple game records must be correctly distinguished with the order and data changing with the games; the history must not always be fixed static samples

features.name: Board size switching
steps: Start a new game each time and perform several swipes
features.expected: All six sizes are recommended for the benchmark. The board matrix, layout size, random generation, movement, merging, and Game Over must all adapt to different N×N; the 4×4 UI must not simply be scaled to other sizes

features.name: Merge and end logic across different board sizes
steps: Merge on both a small board and a large board
Verify that it does not end while merges are still possible and ends when there is no legal move
features.expected: Variable size means all core algorithms must be parameterized; neighbor checks, movement compression, merging, and end detection must not be hard-coded to 4×4

features.name: Theme switching
steps: Switch between system colors / dark theme / light theme
Return to the game and continue operating
features.expected: The screenshot clearly shows only these three themes; after switching, the background, buttons, tiles, and other visuals must update while the board and current game state must not be lost; the system theme should follow the device appearance

features.name: Game guide
steps: Return to the original game state
features.expected: The guide is a separate overlay/page; after closing it should return to the previous game; the text should at least cover four-direction swiping, merging identical numbers, doubling, and the goal of creating larger tiles

features.name: Share the current game
steps: Cancel or choose the target app
features.expected: The system share Intent must be triggered correctly; the share flow must not damage the current game; after cancelling the system share the game keeps its original state

features.name: State after exiting and re-entering the game
steps: Exit via Exit app or the system
Check the current game, the saved state, or the default launch behavior
features.expected: It must be restored according to the target app's actual persistence method; an Activity recreation must not cause the board to change unexpectedly or be regenerated randomly

features.name: Comprehensive full game flow
steps: Then switch to 8×8 and continue the game
features.expected: Comprehensively verify the core state machine: board generation, movement, the single-merge rule, random new tiles, scoring, Undo, pause, persistence, history, themes, Game Over, and variable board sizes must all stay consistent
